text:
Four straight losses would be a bad week anywhere. In Toronto it has turned into a referendum. The headlines in the last two days have Auston Matthews calling out his teammates after the 4-0 loss to New Jersey, William Nylander bringing up trade talk about himself and brushing off critics ("It's not that slumpy," per TSN), and Daily Faceoff asking what the plan is if Matthews ever leaves. The Leafs have been outscored 17-7 in the skid, and the chances back up the scoreboard: they've had 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates). Our playoff race gives them about a 7% chance.

Minnesota walks into that with points in nine straight (7-0-2) and the league's leading goal scorer. Kirill Kaprizov's overtime winner in Montreal was his NHL-leading 17th, and he's on a nine-game point streak. The Wild's own big story sits on the blue line: Sportsnet spent two pieces this week on whether Quinn Hughes stays, while Hughes told The Athletic's Michael Russo he's playing the best hockey of his career. We have Hughes at 44% for two or more points, the highest on either side.

One honest note about the Wild run: it has leaned on the goalie. Minnesota won the chance battle in just one of its last five, and Jesper Wallstedt has covered the gap, .931 over that stretch and nearly 16 goals saved above expected on the season. Toronto goes with Anthony Stolarz over Sergei Bobrovsky, with Chris Tanev out for planned maintenance and Cole McWard in, per Daily Faceoff Toronto.

The Leafs' bright spot is Jack Roslovic: 14 points in 10 games and a spot on the first power-play unit since Kirill Marchenko went down. Toronto takes 4.3 penalties a game, and Minnesota's power play turns those into 0.92 expected goals a night, so discipline is the first thing we'd watch. On our numbers the Wild carry more chances in (3.4 expected goals to 2.73), which is exactly what a team in Toronto's mood can least afford.
headline: The Wild walk into a Leafs referendum
